main_body: A 4x3-tile grass ground patch: a mid-green base with dark-green blobs and sparse small tufts, repeating every 16px
top_band: none (flat ground texture, no standing volume)
evidence: This is a terrain tile, not a standing object. It has no top or front face to judge and none of the four 3/4 failure modes (front elevation, side elevation, top-down slab, rim only) apply. It is a flat ground surface, which is correct for the terrain kind.

style.evidence: The ramp has only about 4 steps: base green, a darker blob green, dark tuft pixels and a few light specks. The Beodeul grass reference has more tones and organic tufts and clumps in several greens. Here the dark patches are blocky, flat-filled blobs of roughly 5x5 px. The base green between the tufts is large and unvaried. The same 16x16 motif repeats identically, so the tiling is obvious and each tile carries only about 4-5 colours. That is thinner and flatter than the reference.
